use_case: One-shot festival or offer poster, containing Indic-script text, generated by a non-designer small-business owner for WhatsApp Status and low-cost print.

design_notes.fairness: Every model receives a byte-identical prompt string. No per-model prompt tuning, no negative prompts, no reference images, no retries. One generation per model per prompt in the primary run (see seeds_and_variance for the variance sub-study).
design_notes.prompt_template: Each prompt follows an identical 5-part structure: [business + scene] + [occasion] + [EXACT TEXT REQUIREMENT, quoted] + [style/format] + [vertical portrait]. This keeps instruction complexity constant so that score differences reflect model capability, not prompt phrasing.
design_notes.text_requirement_phrasing: The exact target string is given in double quotes and the model is told to render it 'exactly as written, with no spelling changes'. This gives us a ground-truth string to score character-by-character, which is what makes Text Fidelity objective rather than a matter of taste.
design_notes.english_control: P10 is a deliberate control: same scene, same structure, same text content as P01, but in Latin script. The TF gap between P10 and the Indic prompts is the Indic Text Penalty (ITP). Without this control we could not distinguish 'bad at text in images' from 'bad at Indic text in images' — and those two findings have completely different implications for a model team.
design_notes.script_coverage: 6 scripts (Devanagari, Tamil, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Telugu, Urdu/Nastaliq) + Latin control. Devanagari is deliberately over-weighted (4 prompts) because it is the highest-volume case, but the non-Devanagari prompts exist to test whether 'Indic support' is really just 'Hindi-ish support' — a distinction that matters enormously for a lab claiming Indian coverage.
design_notes.occasion_coverage: Deliberately spans Hindu (Diwali, Durga Puja), Muslim (Eid), Sikh (Baisakhi), and regional-solar (Pongal, Ugadi) festivals. Most 'Indian' eval sets are implicitly Hindu-default and North-Indian-default; that is itself a representation failure worth measuring.

seeds_and_variance.primary_run: 1 image per (model, prompt) = 10 x 3 = 30 images. This is the set participants rate.
seeds_and_variance.variance_substudy: 3 additional generations for P01 and P05 per model (12 extra images), researcher-scored only, to estimate within-model run-to-run variance on Text Fidelity. Documented separately so headline numbers stay on the clean 1-per-cell design.
seeds_and_variance.rationale: With n=1 per cell we cannot separate model capability from sampling luck on any single prompt. The variance sub-study lets us state how much of an observed per-prompt difference could be noise, which is more honest than silently reporting n=1 as if it were stable.

difficulty_features: Latin numeral + % sign mixed into Devanagari line
prompts.rationale: The single most common real creative an Indian kirana store makes. Deliberately the EASIEST Devanagari case: short, extremely high-frequency words that must appear in any Hindi training data. If a model fails here, it fails everywhere. Paired 1:1 with the English control P10.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a small neighbourhood Indian kirana (grocery) store celebrating Diwali. The poster must prominently display the text "दिवाली धमाका" as the main headline and "50% छूट" as a secondary line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Warm festive lighting, diyas and marigold garlands, shelves of everyday grocery packets visible behind. Bright, high-contrast, eye-catching design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

difficulty_features: words that appear on real signage but are lower-frequency in text corpora
prompts.rationale: The Devanagari stress test. 'मिष्ठान्न भंडार' is exactly what is painted on real sweet-shop boards across North India, and it contains the two things that break text-to-image models: stacked conjunct consonants (संयुक्ताक्षर) and a nukta. Models that produce passable Devanagari on simple words routinely collapse on conjuncts, which is the difference between 'can render Hindi' and 'can render a shop sign'.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a traditional Indian sweet shop. The poster must prominently display the text "मिष्ठान्न भंडार" as the main headline and "ताज़ा मिठाई" as a secondary line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Trays of colourful Indian sweets like laddoo, barfi and jalebi arranged in the foreground, warm golden lighting, festive decorative border. Bright appetising commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

prompts.rationale: Code-mixing is how Indian SMBs actually write — not pure Hindi, not pure English. A model that can only do one script per image fails the real use case. Also tests the rupee glyph, which models frequently render as $ or as a broken box, and that single character error makes a price poster unusable.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a ladies beauty salon advertising wedding-season bridal packages. The poster must prominently display the text "Bridal Makeup" as the main headline, "शादी स्पेशल" as a secondary line, and "₹2999 से" as a price line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Elegant design with soft pink and gold tones, bridal jewellery and mehendi motifs, clean modern layout. Polished commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

prompts.rationale: English loanwords written in Devanagari dominate real Indian signage ('रिपेयरिंग', 'फोटोकॉपी', 'कोचिंग'). These are high-frequency in the physical world but comparatively rare in clean text corpora, so they probe whether the model learned Devanagari as a writing system or memorised a set of Hindi word-images. Also a non-festival, everyday-commerce prompt so the set is not all festival imagery.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a small mobile phone repair shop. The poster must prominently display the text "मोबाइल रिपेयरिंग" as the main headline and "30 मिनट में" as a secondary line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Smartphones, repair tools and a workbench visible, clean blue and white colour scheme, trustworthy professional look. Simple bold commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

difficulty_features: South Indian festival with specific visual iconography (pongal pot, sugarcane, kolam)
prompts.rationale: The generalisation test. If a model's 'Indic' ability is really 'Devanagari-only', this is where it shows. Tamil has ~80M speakers and Tamil Nadu is a major commercial market, so this is not a long-tail curiosity. The Pongal iconography also tests whether the model defaults to North Indian festival visuals regardless of the festival named.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a South Indian textile and saree shop celebrating Pongal. The poster must prominently display the text "பொங்கல் சிறப்பு சலுகை", rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Traditional Pongal imagery including a decorated clay pot, sugarcane stalks and a kolam floor pattern, with colourful silk sarees displayed. Bright festive commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

difficulty_features: NATIVE BENGALI NUMERALS ৫০ rather than Latin 50
prompts.rationale: Contains the nastiest single edge case in the set: native-script numerals. Models almost universally substitute Latin digits even when the prompt specifies Bengali ones. On a price poster that is a correctness failure, not a style choice. Durga Puja is also the highest-commerce festival window in East India, so the commercial stakes are real.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a clothing store in Kolkata celebrating Durga Puja. The poster must prominently display the text "পূজা স্পেশাল" as the main headline and "৫০% ছাড়" as a secondary line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Durga Puja pandal imagery with red and white colours, shiuli flowers and dhak drums, racks of new clothes visible. Bright festive commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

prompts.rationale: A genuinely lower-resource script, included to find the floor. Punjabi is a top-10 Indian language with a large diaspora and high commercial activity, yet it gets far less eval attention than Hindi. The phrase repeats the ੀਆਂ cluster twice, so a model that half-learned the vowel signs will show it visibly in the same image.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a roadside Punjabi dhaba celebrating Baisakhi. The poster must prominently display the text "ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ", rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Baisakhi harvest imagery with wheat fields, bhangra dancers and a dhol drum, hearty Punjabi food like makki di roti and lassi in the foreground. Vibrant yellow and orange festive design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

prompts.business: Small electronics and home appliance shop
prompts.rationale: Telugu has ~83M speakers and Hyderabad is a major commercial centre. Included as a second South Indian script so that a Tamil result cannot be mistaken for a general 'South Indian' result. Short phrase by design — if a model fails on a two-word Telugu string, length is not the excuse.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a small electronics and home appliance shop celebrating Ugadi. The poster must prominently display the text "ఉగాది ఆఫర్", rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Ugadi imagery with mango leaves and neem flowers, television sets, mixers and fans displayed on shelves. Bright clean commercial design with green and yellow tones, suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

difficulty_features: cursive letter joining that changes glyph shape by position
hardest rendering case in the set
prompts.rationale: Two reasons. Technically, RTL + cursive positional shaping is the hardest text-rendering case here, so it establishes the ceiling of difficulty. Substantively, India has ~200M Muslims and Eid is a peak commercial window; an eval set that only covers Hindu festivals would mismeasure India. Testing whether models handle a Muslim-festival prompt with the same quality and without stereotyping is a fairness question, not just a rendering question.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for an Indian bakery and biryani shop celebrating Eid. The poster must prominently display the text "عید مبارک", rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Festive Eid imagery with a crescent moon, lanterns and dates, trays of biryani and sheer khurma in the foreground. Elegant green and gold commercial design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

difficulty_features: deliberately matched to P01 in scene, structure, word count and semantic content
prompts.rationale: CONTROL PROMPT. Identical to P01 in every respect except script. This is the load-bearing element of the experimental design: it separates 'this model is bad at putting text in images' from 'this model is bad at putting INDIC text in images'. The TF difference P10 minus mean(P01..P09) is the Indic Text Penalty. A lab reading our results needs that decomposition to know whether to fix their text renderer or their Indic tokenisation and training data.
prompts.full_prompt: A promotional poster for a small neighbourhood Indian kirana (grocery) store celebrating Diwali. The poster must prominently display the text "DIWALI DHAMAKA" as the main headline and "50% OFF" as a secondary line, rendered exactly as written with no spelling changes. Warm festive lighting, diyas and marigold garlands, shelves of everyday grocery packets visible behind. Bright, high-contrast, eye-catching design suitable for sharing on WhatsApp. Vertical portrait format.

optional_additional_models.why: Ideogram markets text-rendering as its core differentiator, so it is the most informative optional addition: it tells us whether strong Latin text-rendering transfers to Indic scripts at all. Strongly recommended as a 4th model if budget allows.
Widely used open-weight-adjacent baseline; many Indian startups build on FLUX, so its Indic performance has direct downstream impact.
Design/typography-oriented model; relevant because the use case is specifically a typographic artefact.
